objectives.title: Mobile Museum Operation
objectives.desc: To manage the operation and maintenance of the former USS LCS (L)(3) 102 / HTMS NAKHA as a mobile museum.

objectives.title: Honor "The Mighty Midgets"
objectives.desc: To preserve and perpetuate the memory of those officers and men who served so valiantly aboard one of the USS LCS (L) ships and their flagships of the United States Navy, which are informally known as "The Mighty Midgets", and to the H.T.M.S NAKHA of the Royal Thai Navy, especially those officers and men who gave their lives in the service of their country.

objectives.title: Records, Relics & Mementos
objectives.desc: To acquire, preserve, and present the records, relics, and mementos of the Landing Craft Support Vessels.

objectives.title: WWII Pacific Accomplishments
objectives.desc: To inform the public of the World War II accomplishments of the Landing Craft Support ships during operations at Iwo Jima, Okinawa, Philippines, Borneo, China, and the occupation of Japan.

objectives.title: Youth Overnight Stays
objectives.desc: Groups and Boy Scouts can arrange to spend the night or weekend on the LCS 102 at Mare Island Naval Base in Vallejo, California.

objectives.title: San Francisco Bay Cruises
objectives.desc: And to provide cruises open to the public around the San Francisco Bay area.

timeline.title: 1. Birth of the "Yankee Dollar"
timeline.desc: Designed by George Lawley & Sons on an LCI hull, 130 LCS(L) gunboats were built across Massachusetts and Oregon. Laid down Jan 13, 1945 at Commercial Iron Works in Portland and commissioned Feb 17, 1945 under Lt. Richard Jones, LCS-102 earned the nickname "Yankee Dollar" ($1.02).

timeline.title: 2. Battle of Okinawa & Radar Picket #18
timeline.desc: Rushed to the Pacific Theater, LCS-102 fought in the Battle of Okinawa (June 18–30, 1945). Assigned to Radar Picket Station #18 90 miles south of Okinawa, she screened fleet destroyers against relentless kamikaze attacks, earning her WWII Battle Star.

timeline.title: 3. Philippines & Occupation of Japan
timeline.desc: Conducted mine-removal operations at Leyte Gulf when WWII ended, then sailed to Sasebo, Japan—arriving two months after the atomic bomb—where 40 crewmen toured Nagasaki before serving occupation duty in China and Korea.

timeline.title: 4. Reserve Fleet & JMSDF "Himawari"
timeline.desc: Decommissioned in 1946 and redesignated USS LSSL-102 in 1949, she was loaned to postwar Japan in 1953. Serving in the Japanese Maritime Self-Defense Force as JDS Himawari until 1966, she received the lookout deck roof and 81mm mortars still visible onboard.

timeline.title: 5. Royal Thai Navy & Voyage Home
timeline.desc: Transferred to the Royal Thai Navy in 1966 as HTMS Nakha (LSSL-751), serving for 41 years. When WWII veterans found she was the last operational LCS in existence, they secured her repatriation aboard a heavy-lift ship back to San Francisco Bay in 2007.

timeline.title: 6. Mare Island Museum & Historic Landmark
timeline.desc: Berthed at historic Mare Island Naval Shipyard in Vallejo, CA, restored by Navy veterans and volunteers led by Skipper Bill Mason and Gordon Stutrud. Enshrined on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places on October 13, 2015.
